Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels

Source: R/modelterms.R
modelterms.Rd

A standalone, zero-dependency suite of functions to seamlessly manipulate terms objects, formulas, fitted models, and character vectors of term labels.

Usage

as_terms(
  x,
  response = NULL,
  intercept = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  keep.order = NULL,
  env = parent.frame(),
  ...
)

filter_terms(
  x,
  keep = NULL,
  drop = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  require = NULL,
  remove = NULL,
  raw = TRUE,
  response = NULL,
  intercept = NULL,
  ...
)

get_labels(x, ...)

match_labels(x, y, nomatch = c("omit", "pass", "fail"), use.names = TRUE, ...)

get_order(x, use.names = TRUE, ...)

get_variables(x, raw = FALSE, by.term = FALSE, ...)

get_response(x, raw = FALSE, ...)

has_response(x, ...)

has_intercept(x, ...)

Arguments

x, y

an object representing model terms: a terms object, a formula, a fitted model object, or a character vector. In match_labels(), y is the target object whose term labels are matched against.

response

optional response specification for as_terms() and filter_terms(). If NULL (default) or TRUE, retains the existing response of x (or no response if x is a character vector). If FALSE, removes the response variable. If a character string or language object, sets or replaces the response variable.

intercept

optional logical for as_terms() and filter_terms(). If NULL (default), retains the existing intercept status of x (or defaults to no intercept for character vectors unless explicit tokens like "1" or "+1" are present in x). If TRUE or FALSE, explicitly forces or removes the intercept.

data

a data.frame used to resolve . in formulas or shorthand strings.

keep.order

logical. Should terms be kept in their input order rather than sorted by interaction order? Defaults to TRUE for strict term label vectors and FALSE for formulas or length-1 formula shorthands.

env

an environment to attach to the resulting terms object when coercing from a character vector. Defaults to parent.frame().

...

additional arguments passed to terms or as_terms().

keep, drop

a character vector of term labels (matched order-invariantly via match_labels()) or an integer vector of term indices to explicitly retain (keep) or exclude (drop) in filter_terms().

order

an integer vector specifying interaction orders to retain in filter_terms() (e.g., 1L for main effects, 2L for two-way interactions).

require

a character vector of variable names. Only terms containing at least one of these variables are retained.

remove

a character vector of variable names. Any terms containing these variables are excluded.

raw

logical. If FALSE (default in get_variables() and get_response()), returns model expressions (e.g., "log(x2)"). If TRUE (default in filter_terms()), extracts or filters by underlying raw column names (e.g., "x2").

nomatch

character string specifying how to handle unmatched labels in match_labels(): "omit" (default; drops unmatched elements), "pass" (returns NA), or "fail" (throws an error).

use.names

logical. If TRUE (default), match_labels() names the output vector with the input labels from x, and get_order() names the integer vector with the model's term labels.

by.term

logical. If FALSE (default), get_variables() returns a flat character vector across the whole model. If TRUE, returns a named list mapping each term label to its constituent variables.

Value

  • as_terms(), filter_terms(): a terms object.

  • get_labels(), match_labels(): a character vector (named by input labels in match_labels() when use.names = TRUE).

  • get_order(): an integer vector of term orders (named when use.names = TRUE).

  • get_variables(): a character vector (when by.term = FALSE) or a named list of character vectors (when by.term = TRUE).

  • get_response(): a character string (when raw = FALSE), a character vector of variable names (when raw = TRUE), or NULL if no response exists.

  • has_response(), has_intercept(): a scalar logical (TRUE or FALSE).

Details

Three Levels of Model Components

For a model formula such as y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2), this package distinguishes three structural levels:

  1. Term Labels (get_labels(x)): The individual additive components of the model: c("x1", "log(x2)", "x1:log(x2)", "I(x1 * x2)").

  2. Model Variables (get_variables(x, raw = FALSE)): The distinct predictor expressions forming the terms (rows of the "factors" matrix): c("x1", "log(x2)", "I(x1 * x2)").

  3. Raw Variables (get_variables(x, raw = TRUE)): The underlying column names required in data: c("x1", "x2").

Character Input Rules in as_terms()

When x is a character vector, as_terms() distinguishes between a vector of strict term labels and a length-1 formula shorthand:

  • Strict Term Labels (character(n)): If every element (excluding intercept tokens like "1" or "-1") represents strictly a single valid term (e.g., c("b:a", "a", "I(x^2)")), input order and exact interaction notation ("b:a") are preserved by default (keep.order = TRUE).

  • Length-1 Formula Shorthand (character(1)): If x is a single string containing formula operators or . (e.g., ".^2", ".", or "a * b + c + 1"), it is expanded as a right-hand side formula expression (using data if needed) and sorted by interaction order by default (keep.order = FALSE).

  • Invalid Mixed Vectors (length(x) >= 2): If x has length 2 or more and contains any non-single-term expression (such as c("a * b", "c") or c(".", "a")), an informative error is thrown.

Subsetting and Filtering with filter_terms()

filter_terms() serves as a declarative, crash-safe replacement for drop.terms, delete.response, and [.terms:

  • Direct Subsetting: Pass character labels or integer indices to keep (the second argument) or drop to extract or exclude specific terms (order-invariantly) while preserving the intercept and response.

  • Structural Filtering: Use order, require, and remove to filter terms by interaction order or constituent variables.

  • Response & Intercept Control: In both as_terms() and filter_terms(), set response = FALSE to remove the response variable (like stats::delete.response(x)), pass a new variable name to replace it, or set intercept = TRUE / FALSE without crashing even when all predictor terms are dropped.

Examples

# Coercion with as_terms()
t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1"))
get_labels(t1)
#> [1] "b:a" "a"  
has_intercept(t1)
#> [1] TRUE

t2 <- as_terms(".^2", response = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4])
get_labels(t2)
#> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp"
#> [6] "Wind:Temp"   

# Extracting labels, variables, and response at three levels
fml <- log(y) ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2)
get_response(fml, raw = FALSE)
#> [1] "log(y)"
get_response(fml, raw = TRUE)
#> [1] "y"
get_labels(fml)
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" "x1:log(x2)"
get_variables(fml, raw = FALSE)
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE)
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE, by.term = TRUE)
#> $x1
#> [1] "x1"
#> 
#> $`log(x2)`
#> [1] "x2"
#> 
#> $`I(x1 * x2)`
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
#> 
#> $`x1:log(x2)`
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
#> 

# Subsetting, filtering, and modifying response/intercept
fml |> filter_terms("log(x2):x1")
#> log(y) ~ 1 + x1:log(x2)
#> attr(,"variables")
#> list(log(y), x1, log(x2))
#> attr(,"factors")
#>         x1:log(x2)
#> log(y)           0
#> x1               2
#> log(x2)          2
#> attr(,"term.labels")
#> [1] "x1:log(x2)"
#> attr(,"order")
#> [1] 2
#> attr(,"intercept")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"response")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,".Environment")
#> <environment: 0x5c37e20165d0>
fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels()
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
fml |> filter_terms(require = "x2", remove = "x1", raw = TRUE) |> get_labels()
#> [1] "log(x2)"
fml |> filter_terms(drop = "log(x2):x1", response = FALSE)
#> ~1 + x1 + log(x2) + I(x1 * x2)
#> attr(,"variables")
#> list(x1, log(x2), I(x1 * x2))
#> attr(,"factors")
#>            x1 log(x2) I(x1 * x2)
#> x1          1       0          0
#> log(x2)     0       1          0
#> I(x1 * x2)  0       0          1
#> attr(,"term.labels")
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
#> attr(,"order")
#> [1] 1 1 1
#> attr(,"intercept")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"response")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,".Environment")
#> <environment: 0x5c37e20165d0>
fml |> filter_terms(order = 1, response = "yhat", intercept = FALSE)
#> yhat ~ -1 + x1 + log(x2) + I(x1 * x2)
#> attr(,"variables")
#> list(yhat, x1, log(x2), I(x1 * x2))
#> attr(,"factors")
#>            x1 log(x2) I(x1 * x2)
#> yhat        0       0          0
#> x1          1       0          0
#> log(x2)     0       1          0
#> I(x1 * x2)  0       0          1
#> attr(,"term.labels")
#> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)"
#> attr(,"order")
#> [1] 1 1 1
#> attr(,"intercept")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"response")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,".Environment")
#> <environment: 0x5c37e20165d0>

# Order-invariant label matching
match_labels(c("x1", "log(x2):x1", "I(x2 * x1)"), fml, nomatch = "pass")
#>           x1   log(x2):x1   I(x2 * x1) 
#>         "x1" "x1:log(x2)"           NA
